items.text: A secret contact between the US government and the commander of the IRGC has been confirmed. Trump has asked Tehran to surrender at the end of the 60-day deadline for an agreement. The Israeli website Ynet also reported on the IRGC's dominance over the Islamic Republic.

The Minister of Roads stated that about 100 aircraft were damaged in the war, with 8 completely destroyed. Additionally, around 140 private non-military vessels were also damaged. These vessels include local cargo and passenger transport boats used by coastal residents.

The Israeli Prime Minister told Jared Kushner that Israel will not withdraw its forces from Gaza or allow reconstruction until Hamas is fully disarmed. An American general will oversee the disarmament process of Hamas. Hamas demands an end to Israeli attacks and troop withdrawal before disarming.

The documentary drama "Court of History" examines Iran after the Islamic Republic and how to deal with its crimes. The film will be broadcast on Thursday, August 20 at 8:00 PM Tehran time on Iran International. A repeat will air on Friday, August 21 at 11:00 AM.

The Uzbekistan national football team will play against Iran on September 24, 1405 (Persian calendar) in Tashkent. They will then face Argentina in China on September 30 and play against South Korea on October 6. This will be the eighth match between Iran and Uzbekistan during Ghalenoei's era.

The US Department of Defense announced it has ordered 30 US academic institutions to immediately and comprehensively review their academic, financial, and research collaborations with foreign entities of concern to Washington. The stated goal is to prevent unauthorized technology transfer, intellectual property theft, and foreign exploitation of research funded by American taxpayers. The institutions must report their findings and actions by 9 Shahrivar to maintain eligibility for future federal research funding.

The Islamic Consultative Assembly is reviewing a plan called the "Countering Infiltration Plan" that could restrict and securitize communication with foreign media, universities, and institutions. This plan may place Iranian citizens' connections with the world under the supervision of the Ministry of Intelligence. Concerns have been raised about the impact of this plan on the future of Iran's young generation.

Mehdi Ahmadi, the host of the program 'Azad,' has been summoned to the prosecutor's office on charges of spreading falsehoods. He was released on bail according to judicial orders. The 'Azad' media outlet is banned from publishing interviews until further notice.
The spokesperson of the political and press courts jury announced that the manager of the news site Serat News was found guilty by the press court.

Khatoun Bam football team lost 3-0 to CSKA Dushanbe in their first match of the AFC Women's Champions League qualifiers. The goals were scored by Sara Didar and Maryam Dini. Khatoun Bam topped the group with this victory and will play against Al-Nassr Saudi Arabia on Thursday.

Tom Barrack, the US Ambassador to Turkey, strongly condemned the attack on Masrour Barzani, Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Region, and his office in Erbil, calling it a direct threat to regional stability. He wrote on X that aggression against trusted Kurdish allies is unacceptable and Washington will not tolerate such actions. Barrack also expressed full US support for Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's leadership in restoring full national sovereignty.
At 19:30 on Monday, 26 Mordad, a fire broke out in shops around Golestan Municipality Square. Images of the incident have been received. No further details have been announced.

Jared Kushner, Tony Blair, and Nikolay Mladenov met with Benjamin Netanyahu as part of efforts to advance the peace process in Gaza. This meeting took place after their meeting with Hamas representatives. The report was provided by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.

Pierre Poilievre, leader of Canada's Conservative Party, called for the immediate expulsion of agents affiliated with the IRGC from Canada. He also announced coordination for a meeting with Prince Reza Pahlavi. These statements were made at a meeting with Iranians in Vancouver.

Three prisoners sentenced to death in Varamin, Saravan, and Bardasir were spared execution following the consent of the victims' families. This news was reported by Harana News Agency. More details are provided in the continuation of the report.

Behnam Taleblu stated that the 60-day agreement between the Islamic Republic and the US over the Strait of Hormuz lasted only two to three weeks. He considered the diplomatic deadlock predictable. There is a possibility of a military reaction from the Islamic Republic in the coming weeks.

The 25-year prison sentence of Omid Bayat Sarmadi was overturned by the Supreme Court. His case has been referred to a peer branch for re-examination. He was previously sentenced to 25 years in prison by the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

The Islamabad agreement period has ended, and there are few signs of its renewal. One reason is the secret plan of the Islamic Republic to expand the war. This issue was reported by the Wall Street Journal.

The first deputy of Pezeshkian announced that the government, in coordination with security institutions, has set a fourth gasoline price. Mohammad Reza Aref said this plan was supposed to be tested in Kerman province. The 87,000 toman price implemented in Kerman differs from the approved rate.

Ali Al-Zaidi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, announced the formation of a committee to investigate the attack on Masrour Barzani's office. The Kurdistan Region condemned the attack as inconsistent with good neighborliness and criticized the Islamic Republic's behavior. The Kurdistan Region emphasized that this conflict is not part of regional conflicts.

The nonprofit organization FracSquare has requested FIFA's governance committee to declare Gianni Infantino ineligible for re-election as FIFA president. The organization accused Infantino of repeated violations of FIFA's duties and called for an investigation into the awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize to Donald Trump. Infantino's presidency has faced controversies and scandals following these allegations.

About 280 workers at the Siaadan Abhar steel factory have not received one month of wages and several months of insurance payments. Workers at the Iran Shahr steam power plant have also reported wage arrears. Pars Khodro retirees have been waiting for six months for part of their severance pay.

CENTCOM announced that the USS Mason destroyer is enforcing the US Iron Wall blockade against Iran. By August 17, US forces have altered the routes of 64 commercial ships, disabled three ships, and boarded two ships.

The cost of the livelihood basket for an average working-class family has reached 90 million tomans per month. This amount has more than doubled compared to last March when it was 43 million tomans. The income of the majority of the working class is less than half of this amount.
A man in Tehran committed acid attacks on two of his wife's colleagues due to suspicion. He was tried by the Tehran criminal court. This incident took place in Tehran.
Trump confirmed having a direct channel with the IRGC. He threatened Tehran with surrender and bombing Oman. This was mentioned in the audio version of Titraval with Niusha Saremi.

The nonprofit organization Foursquare has requested FIFA to declare Gianni Infantino ineligible for re-election as FIFA president. The group accuses Infantino of repeatedly violating political neutrality and causing multiple controversies. Foursquare also called for an investigation into the awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize to Donald Trump.

Donald Trump said he asked South Korea to help the US regarding Iran, but they refused. He emphasized that the US has 39,000 troops in South Korea protecting them against North Korea. Trump also stated that Iran will not accept the agreement that the US deems necessary.

Donald Trump stated that the United States is not seeking to extend the agreement with the Islamic Republic. He also said that the Islamic Republic will not make the agreement that the US requires. These remarks were made at the White House.

The leader of Canada's Conservative Party criticized the federal government and called for the immediate dismissal of those voluntarily cooperating with the IRGC. He emphasized that conscripts should not be targeted as they are victims of this terrorist organization. He also announced coordination for a meeting with Prince Reza Pahlavi and an official invitation for him to visit Canada.

A senior Iranian official stated that Tehran has given the US only a few weeks to fulfill its commitments under the agreement. After this period, precise and timely military actions will be taken. The political deputy of the IRGC also conditioned the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz on the US fulfilling its commitments.

Kevin Lamour, FIFA's Chief Operating Officer, left the organization less than three weeks after strongly criticizing the canceled plan to sell FIFA competition shares. FIFA confirmed the end of cooperation with Lamour on August 17, 2026, and thanked him. FIFA has not commented on reports of his dismissal.
Donald Trump, responding to a question about Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, said he does not think Oman has behaved very well, but the United States will deal with them very easily.

The film "Bidad" directed by Sohail Beiraghi was released on YouTube without official permission. The film focuses on the ban on women's singing in Iran. The judiciary had previously issued rulings against the filmmakers.

The Appeals Court of Fars Province confirmed the 15-month prison sentence and additional penalties for Mehdi Fathi. He was also sentenced to travel ban, passport cancellation, and two years of prohibition from online activities. This sentence was previously issued by the Revolutionary Court of Shiraz.

Jared Kushner, the US president's special envoy, said Hamas leaders at the rare Cairo meeting expressed positive positions but trust in the group remains difficult and its adherence to commitments must be tested in practice. He added that the process of disarmament and demilitarization of Gaza could begin within 30 days, and reconstruction will not start before that. Kushner also said that if Hamas does not hand over its weapons and tunnels within the next 60 to 90 days, US support for the continuation of Israeli operations will increase.

Many people faced system disruptions and long queues when trying to verify residency and receive ration cards. The Ministry of Cooperatives has requested residency verification by the end of September, otherwise ration card payments will be stopped. The deputy of cooperation in Sistan and Baluchestan advised completing the process online.

Morad Vaisi stated that the Islamic Republic has entered a turbulent 80-day period. This period has started now and will continue until the US elections. He mentioned severe economic pressures, a high possibility of broader conflict with the US, and a renewed uprising by the people.

Morad Veisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, criticized the Islamic Republic's strategy against the US and Israel as fundamentally flawed. He stated that the Islamic Republic assumes the US and Israel are unaware of its plans, which is not true. He also pointed out the mistake of hoping for no attack until the US elections.

Kataib Hezbollah Iraq called Mohammed Shia al-Sudani reckless for pressuring militias and threatened retaliatory action. The group set conditions for disarmament talks. The conditions include the withdrawal of American and Turkish forces and the dissolution of the Peshmerga.

Donald Trump welcomed the idea of declaring the Strait of Hormuz as US territory and said Washington controls the waterway through a naval blockade. He warned that the Islamic Republic is in a difficult economic and military situation. Trump added that Iran still has the ability to cause disruptions, including mining ships' paths.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, identified internal crises and a daily shortage of 15 to 20 million liters of gasoline as major challenges for the Islamic Republic until the US elections. He warned that these crises could lead to social unrest and threaten the regime's survival. He also mentioned the US blockade preventing gasoline imports.

The Asian Football Confederation announced that the deadline for Esteghlal club to introduce a hosting stadium in the Elite League of Asia has ended. The football federations of Iraq and Uzbekistan did not give final approval for Esteghlal's hosting. AFC will make the final decision regarding Esteghlal's hosting stadium.

The Coalition of Iranian Kurdish Political Forces condemned the drone attacks by the Islamic Republic on the office of the Prime Minister of Iraqi Kurdistan and the security organization headquarters. The coalition described these attacks as a violation of Iraq's sovereignty and a threat to the security of the Kurdistan Region. They called for an immediate halt to the attacks and serious action from the Iraqi government and diplomatic countries.

FIFA released images of the 2026 World Cup final between Spain and Argentina from the perspective of the referee, Slavko Vinčić. These images include moments from the match and the referee's interactions with players. More details of these scenes can be found on FIFA's website.

Donald Trump said the Islamic Republic must give up acquiring nuclear weapons and until then, the US will continue economic blockade and control of the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Tehran. He emphasized that despite the Strait of Hormuz being open, the US naval blockade has been effective and prevented the Islamic Republic from using this waterway. Trump added that Washington is ready to intensify its actions if necessary and described the Islamic Republic's economic situation and military capability as very weak.

Donald Trump stated that South Korea rejected the US request to participate in military operations against the Islamic Republic. He criticized this decision and questioned why the US should spend billions defending South Korea while Seoul refuses to support militarily. Trump also said some other US allies, including NATO members, do not participate in protecting the Strait of Hormuz.

The 60-day deadline of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding for a comprehensive agreement between Tehran and Washington has ended. Donald Trump said the Islamic Republic wants an agreement but does not accept the conditions of the US. The US does not intend to extend this memorandum of understanding.

Donald Trump said he asked South Korea to assist the US in a military operation against the Islamic Republic, but Seoul refused. He added that this raises questions about why Washington should defend South Korea against North Korean threats. Report by Niloufar Mansouri, Iran International reporter.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan, in a phone call with Donald Trump, called for continued negotiations with the Islamic Republic to reduce tensions between Washington and Tehran. Erdogan stated that Turkey is ready to support efforts to establish peace. Additionally, the Turkish foreign minister discussed reopening the Strait of Hormuz and maintaining the ceasefire with Abbas Araghchi.

The United Arab Emirates condemned the drone attacks by the Islamic Republic on the Prime Minister's office and the security headquarters of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs called these attacks a violation of Iraq's sovereignty and a threat to regional security. The UAE expressed its support for maintaining security and stability in the Kurdistan Region.

Mike Johnson, Speaker of the US House of Representatives, said he believes the United States is on a path to resolving the war with the Islamic Republic. He added that the conflict with the Islamic Republic has naturally caused gasoline prices to rise and that this situation has been prolonged. Johnson also said he believes a coalition of countries, including NATO allies and Arab countries in the region, will eventually form to keep the Strait of Hormuz open for trade.

The Network for Human Rights Solidarity in Iran stated that the pattern of repression and the current wave of executions continue the policies of the 1980s. The network emphasized the need for accountability of those responsible for the 1988 summer executions and current suppressions in international courts. It also called for uncovering the truth about mass graves and ending pressure on families seeking justice.

According to a Reuters/Ipsos poll, Donald Trump's popularity has dropped to the lowest level of his current presidency. In this poll, 33% approved of his performance while 64% disapproved. This popularity level matches the lowest point of his first presidency in December 2017.

The Yemeni army announced that it carried out 133 military operations against the Houthi militias in the past 24 hours. The group is described as a proxy of the Islamic Republic. The operations targeted the capabilities and forces of the Houthis.

The Federal Court of Canada rejected Salman Samani's request to stop his deportation. Samani had entered Canada on a tourist visa after resigning and claimed he faced the risk of torture in Iran. The judge ruled that Canada's public interest outweighs his claims.

A US State Department spokesperson said Hezbollah is solely responsible for Israel's continued presence in Lebanon and must be disarmed and dissolved. He added this is part of a phased plan for Israeli forces to withdraw from southern Lebanon. This plan is the only practical path to achieving peace and security in the region.

Reuters reported, citing Iranian sources, that the leaders of the Islamic Republic face increasing internal pressure that could lead to nationwide unrest. The main threat is not only economic pressure but also the possibility of renewed widespread unrest. The appointment of Hossein Taeb as commander of the Basij is seen as a sign of the government's concern about this issue.

Noor News criticized the approval of the general framework of the plan to counter infiltration by foreign intelligence services and institutions, calling it ambiguous and problematic. The site warned that the plan could itself become a threat to national security and has serious expert weaknesses. Noor News emphasized that real infiltration occurs through decision-making disruption and information security weaknesses, not through societal elites.

Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains very low despite a slight increase. On Monday, only six cargo ships passed through the waterway. No very large oil tankers or liquefied natural gas carriers have passed during this period.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. A vessel was targeted by an unidentified projectile while exiting the strait. No further details about the incident have been provided.

Democratic and Republican lawmakers in the US Senate criticized Donald Trump's order to reduce joint military exercises with South Korea. Senators described the move as illogical, hasty, and short-sighted. They also expressed concerns about the consequences of this decision.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan emphasized the importance of continuing talks with Iran for diplomacy in a conversation with Donald Trump. The Turkish presidency announced Ankara's readiness to support peace efforts. Jared Kushner described the Iran-US talks as serious and intense, but no agreement has been reached yet.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported that a vessel was hit by an unknown projectile while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The incident damaged the engine room and injured one crew member. Omani coast guard is assisting the crew, and investigations are ongoing.

The draw for the new season of the AFC Champions League 2 was held. Gol Gohar Iran was placed in Group B of the West region and will compete against Al Jazira UAE, Al Muharraq Bahrain, and Arkadag Turkmenistan. The other groups in the West region were also determined.

Mehdi Chamran, head of Tehran City Council, stated that a suitable place for naming after Ali Khamenei has not yet been found in Tehran. Mehrabad Airport and Velayat Park are among the proposed options. There is also a shortage of suitable streets and highways for naming in Tehran.

Fathollah Tavassoli, spokesperson of the Economic Commission of the Iranian Parliament, said that the change of Donald Trump's plane in Istanbul due to a threat from the Islamic Republic marks the beginning of revenge. He called Trump a murderer and mentioned the approval of a law to punish those who kill the leaders of the Islamic Republic. This law has been passed by the parliament and will be mandatory if approved by the Guardian Council.

Erfan Ghaneifard described the threat of Kataib Hezbollah against the Iraqi government as beyond a tactical dispute. He said these groups want to play a decisive role in Iraq's security and impose their political will.

Two businesses, the Hermoso restaurant in Tehran and the Van Wood store in Behbahan, were sealed. The Van Wood store was closed due to publishing immoral content, and its female manager was arrested. The reason for sealing the restaurant has not yet been disclosed.

ILNA reported that a working-class family needs about 90 million tomans monthly income to cover minimum living costs. Many workers' wages in Iran do not even reach half of this amount. This issue was discussed in an interview with Rouzbeh Boulehri.

Qasem Bayat stated that alternative oil transport routes can only compensate for part of the previous exports through the Strait of Hormuz. These solutions are temporary and cannot restore oil export capacity to pre-crisis levels. Gradual reduction of global dependence on Persian Gulf oil may reduce the importance of the Strait of Hormuz in the long term.

The Israeli Prime Minister stated in a meeting with Jared Kushner that Israeli forces will not leave Gaza and reconstruction will not begin until Hamas is fully disarmed. Both sides agreed that an American official will oversee the collection and delivery of Hamas weapons. This report was published by Iran International.

Mohsen Takash, a 33-year-old citizen of Isfahan, has been sentenced to death twice on charges of waging war against God related to last year's December protests. He was tortured during detention, and forced confessions were the basis for his sentence. His family was unaware of his condition for four months, and there is no other evidence against him.

Mohammad Reza Aref described the US presence in the Strait of Hormuz as illegal and said some have claimed ownership of our land. He suggested that Iran should also go to the gulfs and islands around the US and declare its intention to intervene. These remarks were made in response to the US presence in the region.

A citizen in Tehran was arrested for collecting and sending images and coordinates of strategic points to opposition groups. The arrest was carried out by police officers. More details were published by Harana News Agency.

Jasem Khosrji, a citizen from Ahvaz, has been held in Sheiban prison for over five months without a court decision. He was tried in the Ahvaz Revolutionary Court on charges of acting against national security. No verdict has been issued yet, and he has been in uncertainty for more than 160 days.

Hamzeh Darvish, a Sunni prisoner in Lakaan Prison in Rasht, has been deprived of phone contact and visits with his family for three weeks starting from August 5. This action followed his recent beating by prison officers and transfer to the prison infirmary. His family is concerned about his physical condition and the circumstances of his detention.

In Alborz province, village water supply is cut and sold at high prices by tanker. In Kerman, electricity was cut on Monday, August 26. Iranian Marine Installations Company and Steel Alborz Sink Company face salary payment issues and potential closure.

The interrogation session of Shiva Zarei was held at the first interrogation branch of Boein Zahra Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office. She was released on bail after the session. The session took place in the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of Boein Zahra county.

Iran International audiences say the increase in gasoline prices affects the cost of goods and increases household financial pressure. They believe this price hike will intensify inflation and shrink people's livelihoods. An interview was conducted with Baharan Azadi, a member of Iran International's editorial team.

Farahnaz Espad, a journalist and presenter at Iran International, passed away at the age of 37 after battling cancer for two years. She had been working with Iran International for eight years and was unable to work due to her illness. Iran International expressed condolences to her family and audience.

A member of the Supreme Council of Provinces warned that 400 villages in South Khorasan are supplied with water by tanker. Excessive groundwater extraction and reduced rainfall have caused a drop in aquifer levels and land subsidence. This crisis has affected farmers' livelihoods and led to rural migration.

The head of Esteghlal Football Club's organization announced that the Asian Football Confederation opposed the team's hosting in Iraq and Uzbekistan. Esteghlal's proposal to hold matches in these two countries was rejected. The final decision on the venue will be announced in the next few hours.

A business unit in Isfahan was closed due to selling T-shirts with images deemed against trade regulations by the police. The police declared these designs as violating the rules. This action was taken by the relevant authorities.

Ali Shirazi stated that the President of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq has been added as a communication channel between the IRGC and Washington. This indicates that Trump is seeking dialogue with centers of power and military commanders of the Islamic Republic to achieve a lasting agreement.

Foolad Khuzestan club announced that Ramin Rezaeian has joined the team. Rezaeian said goodbye to Esteghlal fans on Instagram and emphasized that he fought for them until the last day of his contract. Upon arriving in Ahvaz, he said he owes the World Cup to the city and has come to make the fans happy.

Alireza Jafarzadeh, a master's student in international political economy at Beheshti University, has been sentenced to a temporary suspension from studies for two semesters. His disciplinary ruling was finalized by the university's appeals council. The proposal for his expulsion has also been referred to the Student Affairs Organization for decision.

Several employees of the Pars Oil and Gas Company held protests in various sections and offshore platforms in the South Pars and Asaluyeh region. They demanded the removal of salary caps, full payment of wages, and revision of minimum wages. They also requested not to merge the oil pension fund with other pension funds and called for addressing their other demands.

The governor of Khorasan Razavi attributed the December 2025 protests to enemy interference. He also acknowledged responsibilities and structural mistakes in this regard. He emphasized the need to create an environment of interaction with the youth.

Donald Trump posted an image of the Strait of Hormuz map and parts of Iran, the Persian Gulf, and the Sea of Oman on the Truth Social network. The image includes the phrase "New American Territory" and the Strait of Hormuz is circled. Trump did not provide any further explanation about the image.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, said the enemy seeks to create chaos, terror, and separatist actions. He added that the enemy intends to exploit potential dissatisfaction regarding gasoline. Ghalibaf emphasized that resolving this challenge can disappoint the enemy.

A mother in Markazi province reported her family's inability to afford the medication for her 36-year-old child with ALS. The cost of 13 prescribed ampoules is about 65 billion tomans, which the family cannot cover even by selling a three-billion-toman house. Efforts to seek help from medical centers and various institutions have only resulted in promises of 500 to 600 million tomans in aid.

Kazem Gharibabadi reacted to Donald Trump's image of the Strait of Hormuz, calling it an illusion. He stated that this illusion will soon be corrected. Trump had posted an image titled "New American Territory" showing the Strait of Hormuz.

Today, Tuesday, 27 Mordad, a group of applicants for the land of Shahid Madani Cooperative in Tabriz protested the prolonged uncertainty of their case in front of the East Azerbaijan Governor's Office.
A resident of Isfahan stated that he paid nearly one million tomans for breakfast groceries. This amount exceeds his entire daily wage. This indicates a sharp increase in food costs.

The asphalt paving operation on the bed of the Aligudarz River was carried out without a permit and has been halted until a technical decision is made. The municipality made a mistake in this operation. The Lorestan Regional Water Company issued a written warning and experts are investigating the matter.

The Speaker of the Iranian Parliament criticized the government's increase in gasoline prices, calling it an uncalculated measure and claiming that the enemy has planned to create unrest. He emphasized that the gasoline shortage problem should be solved with comprehensive and smart planning. Masoud Pezeshkian also acknowledged the impact of the US naval blockade on gasoline imports.

Nechirvan Barzani, the head of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, has made efforts to establish contact between the US and the IRGC. These contacts began in early March to reduce tensions between Tehran and Washington. The Kurdistan Region spokesman confirmed the news, but Iran and the IRGC have denied it.

Last night, a group of citizens gathered in front of Sanandaj prison demanding the halt of Kaveh Rafusheh's death sentence. He had been sentenced to death for murder. His execution was carried out early Tuesday morning, August 17, at Sanandaj prison.

The Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson called Iran's request for the Red Cross to intervene in the Iranian pilots' issue a media trick. Qatar stated that its invitation to the Iranian delegation to review the case remains valid. Iran has not yet responded to this invitation.

The President of the United States, Donald Trump, on Tuesday, 27 Mordad, in a post on Truth Social, again called the Strait of Hormuz 'territory of the United States'. He published a graphic image in which the Strait of Hormuz is marked as 'new territory' of the United States. Trump had previously, in a speech, introduced this waterway as part of US territory.

Frequent power outages in Falard county, Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari province, have caused financial damage to a baker. This issue is shown in a video published on social media. The damage caused by these outages has attracted attention.

Donald Trump posted an image on the social network Truth Social showing a map of the Strait of Hormuz and parts of Iran, the Persian Gulf, and the Sea of Oman. The image includes the phrase "New American Territory" and highlights the Strait of Hormuz with a circle. This occurred amid ongoing tensions between the Islamic Republic and the United States in the region.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that the water flow in Mahmoudabad city, Mazandaran province, has been cut off for some time. He said that not even a drop of water is flowing in the pipes. This issue has caused concerns in the city.

Uzi Dayan, former deputy chief of staff of the Israeli army, stated that Israel cannot rely on the US regarding Iran and must rely on itself. He emphasized that Israel fights for its vital and existential needs and must be fully prepared defensively and offensively. Dayan added that conditions may change at any moment, and Israel must be fully ready.

Trump stated that there are no ongoing or planned negotiations with the Islamic Republic of Iran. He said the naval blockade continues with full force and the Strait of Hormuz is open and active. Additionally, all naval mines have been cleared or detonated.

Donald Trump stated that there are no ongoing or planned negotiations with the Islamic Republic. He also said the naval blockade remains fully in place and the Strait of Hormuz is open and active. All naval mines have been cleared or detonated.

Reuters reported that Iran's oil exports have dropped to less than 300,000 barrels per day this month. Homayoun Falakshahi attributed this decline to the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade is being seriously enforced.

Mohammadreza Zafarghandi, the Minister of Health, stated that 50,000 deaths annually are attributed to air pollution. He compared this number to 20,000 deaths caused by accidents. The Minister emphasized that health issues require attention to social and environmental factors.

Six commercial units in the counties of Nikshahr and Tabas were sealed by order of judicial and law enforcement authorities. Some of these closures in Tabas were attributed to the publication of images and videos related to non-compliance with hijab in cyberspace.

The Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman stated that Iranian warplanes entered Qatar's airspace to target its sovereignty. After the pilots did not respond to communications, they were engaged according to rules of engagement. Qatar recovered the body of one pilot and called Iran's statements baseless.

Jafar Panahpour, a wildlife cameraman, released a video showing five gray wolves in Golestan National Park. He explained that wolves live and hunt in family packs. These cohesive groups play an important role in maintaining ecosystem health.

A citizen from Gilan province reports frequent power outages during hot and humid days in the villages of the province. These outages occur simultaneously with the activities of rice farmers. He criticizes this situation.

Hassan Hassanzadeh, commander of Tehran province's IRGC, said people have participated in the war with a sense of responsibility from the beginning. He emphasized that people's support for the system and revolution will continue. This presence will last until the enemy becomes discouraged from continuing the war.
Mohammad Baqer Kharazi, a cleric and political activist, has been detained for about six days by order of the Special Clerical Prosecutor's Office in Qom. He remains in custody.

On Wednesday, 28 Mordad at 9 PM Tehran time, an Instagram live with Amir Pouria will discuss underground cinema in Iran. The conversation is prompted by the online release of the film "Bidad" by Sohail Beiraghi. The film is about a young singer who resists the ban on women singing in Iran.

Mohammad Mokhber stated that the Islamic Republic is logical and open to dialogue but does not confuse negotiation with surrender. He said the Islamic Republic is not warlike but will not retreat from self-defense. Mokhber also emphasized that pressure and sanctions cannot break the will of the Iranian people.

Ali Madanizadeh, the Minister of Economy, stated that the top priority of the Islamic Republic is to increase economic resilience. He emphasized the need to minimize the impact of enemy pressures on the economy. He also highlighted the importance of maximum public participation in the economy through saving and investment.
Vahid reported that a missile alert was announced in Dubai at 18:52. This news was released urgently. The exact time of the event has been specified.

A resident of Mahmoudabad reported that the electricity at his home was cut off for the third time in one day. This was reported by sending a video to Iran International. Power outages have been repeated in this area.

The National Emergency Crisis and Disaster Management Authority of the UAE announced that the country's air defense systems detected a missile threat. The threat was targeting the country. People have been advised to stay in a safe place and follow official alerts.

Abbas Araghchi stated that Masoud Pezeshkian proposed Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf for the negotiations. Araghchi said Pezeshkian insisted that Ghalibaf's name be listed as the head of negotiations in the protocol. Araghchi also mentioned that the Americans initiated the proposal for negotiations.
